When both factors are whole numbers, then:

$\blueE{\text{factor}} \times \blueE{\text{factor}} = \maroonD{\text{multiple}}$

###Factors of $45$

$\begin{align}
\blueE{1} \times \blueE{45} &= \maroonD{45}\\\\
\blueE{3} \times \blueE{15} &= \maroonD{45}\\\\
\blueE{5} \times \blueE{9} &= \maroonD{45}\\\\
\end{align}$

All of the shaded numbers in the table are factors of $\maroonD{45}$.
The shaded numbers on the hundred chart are only the factors of $45$.
